description:
Create a new `jmap-jscontact-types` crate containing typed RFC 9553 sub-types as opt-in helpers for callers, then consume it from `jmap-contacts-types`. The public `ContactCard` struct keeps its 22 `Option<serde_json::Value>` fields as the wire-format anchor; consumers obtain typed views via `serde_json::from_value`.

## Strategy decision (resolved 2026-05-10)

The original epic proposed adding `jscontact.rs` directly inside `crate-jmap-contacts-types/src/`. On 2026-05-10 this was changed to **extract to a new `jmap-jscontact-types` crate** — mirroring the parallel decision for jscalendar (see JMAP-yfpq's strategy resolution and the jscalendar extraction epic).

Rationale:
1. **Spec-aligned**. RFC 9553 (JSContact) is a standalone IETF spec consumed by JMAP Contacts and potentially other future JMAP extensions or non-JMAP consumers. The Rust crate graph should mirror the spec dep graph.
2. **Pre-publish window**. Creating the types directly in a new crate is free now; consolidating later (extraction from contacts-types) would be expensive.
3. **Cookie-cutter symmetry**. With `jmap-jscalendar-types` becoming a foundation crate, having `jmap-jscontact-types` as its sibling is the symmetric pattern. Both are "RFC-defined JSON sub-types, no JMAP dep, consumed by JMAP extension-types crates."

This decision affects this epic's scope but does not affect the TYPE WORK — the 22 typed sub-types still get created, they just live in a new crate from day one rather than inside contacts-types.

## Scope (updated)

In scope:
- Create new `jmap-jscontact-types` crate at `crate-jmap-jscontact-types/`.
- Define 22 typed sub-types covering the ContactCard sloppy fields: Name, Nickname, Organization, Title, SpeakToAs, EmailAddress, OnlineService, Phone, LanguagePref, Address, CryptoKey, Directory, Link, Media, Anniversary, PersonalInfo, Localization, RelatedTo, Calendar, SchedulingAddress, Note, Keyword.
- Each typed sub-type: `Serialize + Deserialize + Debug + Clone + PartialEq`, `#[non_exhaustive]`, doc-comment citing the relevant RFC 9553 section.
- Round-trip tests for each type using hand-written RFC 9553 example JSON fixtures (oracle-independent).
- `jmap-contacts-types` adds a path-dep on `jmap-jscontact-types` and re-exports the typed sub-types so callers can do `jmap_contacts_types::Name` symmetrically with the calendars pattern.
- New crate has `AGENTS.md`, `PLAN.md`, `README.md` mirroring the foundation type-crate idiom (jmap-types AGENTS.md is the closest model — not jmap-mail-types, because jscontact-types has no JMAP dep).
- Update workspace `Cargo.toml` to add the new crate as a workspace member.
- Update workspace `AGENTS.md` crate map and dependency tree.
- Update `crate-jmap-contacts-types/PLAN.md`: replace §10 "current sloppy-Value rationale" notes with a pointer to `crate-jmap-jscontact-types/PLAN.md` for the hybrid-design rationale.

Out of scope:
- Changing the `ContactCard` public struct or its 22 sloppy fields.
- Changing the JMAP wire format.
- Touching `jmap-contacts-server` or `jmap-contacts-client` (they continue to consume `jmap-contacts-types` and pick up the typed sub-types transparently via re-export).
- Adding semantic validation (kept in handlers / callers per existing policy).

## New crate properties

- Crate name: `jmap-jscontact-types`
- Directory: `crate-jmap-jscontact-types/`
- Dependencies: `serde`, `serde_json` only. No async, no JMAP dep.
- `#[forbid(unsafe_code)]` at lib.rs root.
- License: workspace inheritance.
- MSRV: workspace inheritance.
- Cookie-cutter shape: **foundation-shaped** (model on `jmap-types` / `jmap-jscalendar-types`), NOT a member of the extension-types canonical family.

## Acceptance criteria

- `jmap-jscontact-types` exists and compiles cleanly.
- Each of the 22 typed sub-types round-trips through `serde_json::from_value` / `to_value` with an RFC 9553 example.
- `jmap-contacts-types` re-exports the 22 types at the top level for caller symmetry with jmap-calendars-types.
- Workspace AGENTS.md updated to include the new crate in the crate map and dep tree.
- `cargo doc --all-features --no-deps -p jmap-jscontact-types` clean.
- `cargo doc --all-features --no-deps -p jmap-contacts-types` clean.
- `cargo clippy -p jmap-jscontact-types --tests -- -D warnings` clean.
- `cargo clippy -p jmap-contacts-types --tests -- -D warnings` clean.
- `cargo test --workspace` clean.

## Source material

- RFC 9553 (JSContact) full text: `~/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec/references/rfc9553.txt`
- `crate-jmap-jscalendar-types/` (after extraction epic lands) — reference pattern for new-foundation-crate shape: Cargo.toml, AGENTS.md, PLAN.md, README.md, lib.rs layout.
- `crate-jmap-calendars-types/PLAN.md` (post-extraction) — model for how contacts-types' PLAN.md should reference the new crate.
- `crate-jmap-contacts-types/PLAN.md §10` — current sloppy-Value rationale.

## Decomposition hint

Split into one bead per RFC 9553 section family so each child fits in one safe pass:
- .1 Scaffolding: Create new jmap-jscontact-types crate (Cargo.toml, lib.rs, AGENTS.md, PLAN.md, README.md, workspace member).
- .2 Names family: Name, Nickname, SpeakToAs.
- .3 Organizational family: Organization, Title.
- .4 Communication family: EmailAddress, OnlineService, Phone.
- .5 Addressing family: Address.
- .6 Calendaring family: Calendar, SchedulingAddress.
- .7 Personal family: Anniversary, PersonalInfo, LanguagePref, Note, Keyword.
- .8 Linking/Media family: Link, Media, Directory, CryptoKey, RelatedTo.
- .9 Localization family: Localization.
- .10 Consumer migration: jmap-contacts-types path-dep + re-export + PLAN.md pointer.
- .11 Workspace docs: AGENTS.md crate map + dep tree update.

Each child's completeness gate: typed sub-types for that family round-trip against RFC 9553 examples, doc comments cite the relevant section.

## Coordination

- **JMAP-lbdy** (extras-preservation policy) is blocked by this epic. After this lands, JMAP-lbdy.5 (jmap-contacts-types) will sweep the extras pattern over the new typed sub-types (in jmap-jscontact-types) and the existing ContactCard. Do NOT pre-emptively add the extras pattern in this epic; leave that for lbdy.5.
- **JMAP-yfpq** (parallel for tasks-types) shares the cookie-cutter shape but is independent. Both depend on no other epic.
- **jscalendar extraction epic** is conceptually parallel but mechanically independent — sehw can land in any order relative to it.

## Why no extraction step

For jscalendar, the typed sub-types already existed inside jmap-calendars-types; the parallel epic is a pure extraction. For jscontact, the typed sub-types DO NOT yet exist anywhere. This epic creates them directly in the new crate — no extraction phase needed.

title: EPIC: create new jmap-jscontact-types crate with typed RFC 9553 sub-types
